events.text:
`slugify("Hello,  World!")` now returns `"hello-world"`, and all 4 tests pass.

**Cause:** `slugify` swapped each non-alphanumeric character for its own hyphen. Runs like `",  "` became `---`, and the trailing `!` left a hyphen at the end.

**Fix** (`textutils.py`): it now replaces each run of non-alphanumeric characters with a single hyphen (`[^a-z0-9]+`) and trims hyphens from both ends. I also added the type hints the project conventions require.

**Test** (`tests/test_textutils.py`): I added `test_regression_slugify_collapses_separators`. It covers the reported input plus a few edge cases: hyphens and underscores at the start and end, input that is only punctuation (gives `""`), and an empty string. It failed before the fix with `'hello---world-' != 'hello-world'` and passes now. I didn't change any existing tests.

One related problem I left alone: `word_count` splits on single spaces, so `word_count("a  b")` returns 3 instead of 2. Changing `text.split(" ")` to `text.split()` would fix it if you want.

Nothing is committed.
